title: From a list of integers, keep only numbers greater than a threshold and convert each to its `String` form (`filter(...).map(String::valueOf)`).
shortTitle: From a list of integers, keep only numbers greater than a threshold and convert each to its String form

s1_definition.profdef: You filter numbers above a threshold, then map the survivors to strings: `stream().filter(n -> n > threshold).map(String::valueOf).toList()`, producing a list of string representations of the qualifying numbers.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya keeps only the amounts over a cutoff and then writes each as text for a display.
s1_definition.oneliner: `filter(n -> n > t).map(String::valueOf)` keeps big numbers and turns each into a string.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** You filter numbers above a threshold, then map the survivors to strings: `stream().filter(n -> n > threshold).map(String::valueOf).toList()`, producing a list of string representations of the qualifying numbers.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya keeps only the amounts over a cutoff and then writes each as text for a display.

**One line to remember:** `filter(n -> n > t).map(String::valueOf)` keeps big numbers and turns each into a string.

sections.s2_technical:
`filter(n -> n > threshold)` keeps only elements strictly above the threshold, and `map(String::valueOf)` converts each surviving Integer to its decimal string. Ordering matters for clarity and efficiency: filtering first means you only convert the numbers you actually keep, avoiding wasted string allocations for discarded elements.

`String::valueOf` is a static method reference that safely handles the conversion, including nulls by producing the string "null" if a null slipped through — so I filter nulls first if the list can contain them. The result is a `List<String>`.

The senior nuance is operation order for performance: always filter before map so expensive transformations only run on the retained elements. I decide whether the threshold is strict or inclusive, and I handle nulls explicitly. This filter-then-map shape is one of the most common stream pipelines, and placing the cheap, selective filter first is a simple but real optimisation.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — A display at the National Bank of India shows, as text, only the transaction amounts above a reporting threshold.

This is exactly what filter-then-map does — it keeps the large amounts and renders each as a string.

The code defines a `ThresholdService.aboveAsText` method and a demo.
sections.s5_journey:
Input: 5000, 500, 12000, 800, 20000 with a threshold of 1000.

Step 1: The null filter passes all values.

Step 2: filter keeps values strictly above 1000, dropping 500 and 800.

Step 3: The survivors 5000, 12000, 20000 remain.

Step 4: map converts each to its string form, giving "5000", "12000", "20000".

```
INFO: Above 1000 as text: [5000, 12000, 20000]
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Above-Threshold Text View ═══

  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ──text list──→ display
  │ amounts  │→│ ThresholdService │
  │ + cutoff │ │ filter→map       │
  └──────────┘ └──────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — filter then map ═══

  ┌─ order matters ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ filter(n > threshold) FIRST → only convert kept elements    │
  │ map(String::valueOf) → decimal text                         │
  │ String.valueOf(null) → "null" → filter nulls first          │
  │ strict > vs >= : decide boundary                            │
  │ cheap/selective filter before expensive map = optimisation  │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │          ThresholdService     │
  │  + aboveAsText(List, int): List │ filter(>t)→map(valueOf)
  └───────────────────────────────┘

  Call chain:
  1. stream().filter(nonNull).filter(n > threshold)
  2. map(String::valueOf)
  3. toList()
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To keep numbers above a threshold and render them as text I filter first and map second. The filter keeps only values strictly above the threshold, and then map with String valueOf converts each surviving integer to its decimal string, producing a list of strings. At the National Bank of India this backs a display that shows only transaction amounts above a reporting cutoff, rendered as text.

The deliberate detail is the operation order: I filter before I map so that the string conversion only runs on the numbers I actually keep, rather than wasting allocations converting values that will be discarded. On a small list this is negligible, but as a habit it is a real optimisation because the cheap, selective operation runs first and shrinks the work for the expensive one.

The senior point I add is null handling and boundary clarity. String valueOf would turn a null into the text "null" rather than throwing, so if the list can contain nulls I filter them out first, and I decide explicitly whether the threshold is strict or inclusive since that changes which values survive. This filter-then-map shape is one of the most common pipelines I write, and getting the order and the edge cases right is what makes it both efficient and correct.
